inputPreconditions: Observation and Gold use evaluationSchemaVersion 2 and have the same caseId.
attemptBudget is a non-negative integer; no-tool Gold has no allowed sequences.
Tool-positive Gold has unique non-empty sequences; each has unique step IDs and exactly one final terminal step.
Every prior-output binding references an earlier step in the same sequence.
Runtime contract IDs are unique; every Gold step references a present identity/operation-compatible contract with frozen integer acceptance statuses.
The public scorer throws on an input-precondition violation instead of turning bad data into a model outcome.
semanticInvariants: Only executor-bound attempts contribute to triggeredAttempt, observedAttemptCount, and FCR_attempt facts.
A complete chain is an ordered allowed-sequence match with per-step identity, operation, arguments, prior-output binding, exact referenced-contract acceptance, and terminal semantics.
Operation normalization distinguishes none, value, conflict, and invalid results; conflict or invalid operations never match a Gold none/exact operation.
Unexpected, duplicate, or over-budget attempts can preserve completeChainSuccess but make strictChainExact false, positiveOvercall true, and ToolSPL smaller.

A forbidden wrong-family, typed wrong-terminal, or genuinely premature accepted terminal before a correct terminal prevents later repair from creating terminalSelectionCorrect or completeChainSuccess.

The evaluation prefix stops at the earliest Gold terminal whose own arguments, binding, and exact referenced RuntimeToolContract acceptance are valid; prerequisite failures at that horizon cannot be washed out by a later retry.
Without a terminal horizon, failed positives stop at budget or turn completion.
terminalAttemptIndex is an executor-bound ordinal identifying the horizon/complete terminal, otherwise the Qi match, otherwise an in-prefix raw terminal candidate.
Post-terminal behavior does not change decision metrics, but raw trace and infrastructure facts remain preserved for Integration.
M0 never produces final formal metric eligibility.
formalDataBlockers: The frozen v1 ToolPromptEvalCase schema still represents allowedSequences as string[][] rather than per-sequence typed predicates.
The frozen v1 schema still shares expectedFollowupActions and expectedKnowledgeCalls across branches.
No formal Gold v2 revision/tag or closed skill_view versus skill_view_by_id RuntimeToolContract is available in this branch.
